issues.description: Class name mismatch between the problem statement (UML and tasks) and the solution repository: the exercise and UML require concrete animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (students are asked to implement Seal, Pig, Goat and their methods). In the solution repository the corresponding implementations are provided under different class names: SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat (files SpaceSeal.java, SpacePig.java, SpaceGoat.java). Meanwhile the files Seal.java, Pig.java, and Goat.java in the solution repository are empty. This inconsistency (expected names Seal/Pig/Goat vs. actual implementation names SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat) will confuse students and can break automated tests or instructor expectations that look for the exact class names Seal, Pig, and Goat.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure the solution and repository use the same class identifiers as specified in the problem statement. Either: (a) rename or add classes so that concrete implementations exist with the expected names Seal, Pig, and Goat (e.g. create Seal.java that implements the same behavior as SpaceSeal), or (b) update the problem statement/tests to accept the SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat names. A minimal, student-friendly fix is to add small wrapper classes with the expected names that delegate to the existing Space* implementations (for example: public class Seal extends SpaceSeal { public Seal(String name){ super(name); } }). This preserves the provided implementations while matching the required identifiers and avoiding test failures.
